public_rationale: The part that can be checked is his statement that Anthropic's and OpenAI's $200 plans let users consume $8,000 to $14,000 a month. In a post on August 23, 2026, SemiAnalysis said it ran a test in June 2026. That test found that Anthropic's $200 plan can yield up to $8,000 a month in tokens, and OpenAI's $200 plan up to $14,000 a month, if all weekly limits were used up on long-horizon tasks (e1). A summary published June 16, 2026, before his post, reports the same figures. It describes them as API-equivalent token value from extended coding and agentic sessions (e2). The same summary says the figures are API-equivalent cost, not the labs' actual compute cost (e3). The contract reads 'burn' as value at API prices, so this caveat does not change the result. The June test falls inside the target period of June 1 to July 28, 2026. His view that this is 'not a business model' is opinion and is not graded.
limitations: The figures are maximum values at API list prices under full use. They do not show the labs' actual cost of serving these users.
The evidence does not show how much typical subscribers use.
The full SemiAnalysis report is paywalled, so its method could not be checked. Both evidence items trace back to that one test.
The evidence does not show whether the limits stayed the same through the rest of the target period after the June test.
The opinion that AI code generation is 'not a business model' is not assessed.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI code generation is not a business model; Anthropic and OpenAI let users burn $8,000–$14,000 a month for a $200 subscription.

statement.excerpt: The ability to generate code in a mindless and expensive way that sometimes works and may or may not make developers an indeterminate level of more-productive is not a business model, a point made more obvious by the fact that Anthropic and OpenAI allow users to burn $8000 to $14,000 a month for $200.
statement.document_title: The More You Buy, The More You Lose

from_speaker: Anthropic and OpenAI allow users to burn
our_interpretation: The checkable part is factual: the $200-a-month plans from Anthropic and OpenAI let a user consume about $8,000 (Anthropic) to $14,000 (OpenAI) a month of usage. Read plainly, the value is measured at the companies' published API prices, which matches the experiment the post links to.
'Not a business model' is his opinion and is not graded.
'Burn' is read as consumption valued at API list prices, not the labs' internal compute cost.
The claim is in the present tense, in a post dated July 28, 2026. The target period is June 1 to July 28, 2026: the most recent period public measurements could cover before the post.
criteria.support_condition: A measurement covering the target period shows that a maxed-out $200 plan yields roughly $8,000 a month at API prices for Anthropic and roughly $14,000 for OpenAI.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Measurements covering the target period show that $200 plans yield far less (for example, a few thousand dollars a month at API prices), or that no such usage was possible.
